ctx.x: So you’re conductor, not drummer? You didn’t do both duties?

Oh yeah. I let Don do the conducting. I let Don do the tempos. I started the tempos off. He was good with it. He knew the tempos too. items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: he has played on numerous sessions with Nelson Riddle and Louis Bellson.

ctx.x: Count Basie recognized his talent and was able to keep Sweets from 1938-1950.
His unique sound can be heard behind the classic recordings of Frank Sinatra and he has played on numerous sessions with Nelson Riddle and Louis Bellson.
Jazz lovers can hear Sweets on hundreds of records with these various ensembles and under his own name. Mr. Edison will receive an Honorary Doctorate from Hamilton College in May of 1996.
